title: Rugiland
capsule: Rugiland was the kingdom of the Germanic Rugii north of the Danube in what is now Lower Austria, centered near Favianis (modern Mautern), constituted under King Flaccitheus by c. 455–467. His son Feletheus (r. c. 475–487) maintained uneasy relations with Odoacer's Italy; the ecclesiastical mission of Severinus of Noricum, documented in Eugippius's Life, offers the main contemporary record of the kingdom. In 487 Odoacer launched a preemptive invasion, defeated the Rugii, and had Feletheus and his wife Giso executed in Ravenna; surviving Rugii joined Theodoric the Great's Ostrogothic forces crossing into Italy in 489, and the Rugii ceased to exist as a distinct polity.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core zone north of the Danube bend is attested by Eugippius and Cassiodorus; its precise extent eastward toward Pannonia is uncertain and subject to scholarly debate.
